newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-IPE Brent fall temporary if support holds.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-IPE Brent fall temporary if support holds.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* Analysts see downside for crude as temporary depending on whether trendline support at $18.18 is held by the close today.
* The failure of front month Brent to break above downtrend creates a very powerful line of resistance for the future.
* Gas oil seen technically and fundamentally negative with triple top at $167.75/$168 seen capping any further upside.
Profit-taking after this week's run up and ahead of the U.S. holiday this weekend triggered a typical Thursday correction as brokers squared positions.
But analysts see the downside for Brent crude as temporary, depending on whether trendline support at $18.18 is held by the close today.

"Key trendline support is at $18.18. With New York closed Brent may be quiet today, but still a close below this level could trigger some big move back towards $17.50 early next week," said Tom James, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Rouse.
"Technically I would prefer to be a cautious short today, but I would add to that short position only if Monday's trading confirms that the big drop was not just a pre-4th or July event," he added.

GNI research said in their daily report, "The failure of front month Brent to break above the downtrend creates a very powerful line of resistance for the future with three well spaced points of contact (between the June 9 high of $24.90, May 16s $20.60 high and Wednesday's $18.96 high). The short-term uptrend line (from June 20's $17.48 low) clearly acted as support on Thursday, but is nowhere near as strong as its negative brother".

Gas oil is seen technically and fundamentally negative with a triple top at $167.75/$168 seen capping any further upside and a close below trendline support at $164.75 today would leave the market with and increasingly bearish undertone, analyst said.
James said, "The almost perfect triple-top over the last three trading days at $167.75/$168 on the July chart leaves the market looking rather bearish".

However, despite the short term bearishness technical indicators continue to point room for a further upside to most markets. RSIs across the IPE and NYMEX markets remain in neutral territory but momentum indicators remain bullish with trendline supports in place on both crude and products.
August Brent on SIMEX was quoted at $18.10/18.28, in line with the London close of $18.21 after falling 71 cents.
Brokers said the fall in IPE Brent was mainly the result of profit-taking by traders, although news that Iraqi crude exports were a step closer to resuming was also a factor.
But brokers expected levels to move up rather than down, after bouncing off a trendline support of $18.18.
